# Appeal of Denial – ACL Reconstruction (CPT 29888)

**RE: Request for Reconsideration of Adverse Benefit Determination**
**Member:** Quinn Grant
**Member ID:** W553544386
**Reference Number:** POC-87E365CAED-66145
**Date of Denial Notice:** August 2, 2026
**Plan:** UnitedHealthcare (Commercial/ACA), Minnesota
**Governing Policy:** Surgery of the Knee (Commercial), UnitedHealthcare — https://www.uhcprovider.com/content/dam/provider/docs/public/policies/comm-medical-drug/surgery-knee.pdf (effective 2026-06-01)

Dear UnitedHealthcare Appeals Department,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of my ACL reconstruction (CPT 29888), noted above. My surgeon, Dr. Duval, has documented that this surgery is medically necessary, and I am asking the plan to reconsider its decision.

## Why I Am Appealing

The denial notice states that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I want to walk through what my records actually show, and I want to be clear and direct with the plan about what its own policy does and does not say.

**What my records show:**
- I have had 24 months of progressive knee pain that did not resolve with rest.
- I completed 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy (20 visits, April 12, 2026 – June 21, 2026) focused on range of motion and quadriceps strengthening, with bracing. This is documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- I took NSAIDs for 6 months without adequate relief.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on April 17, 2026, which gave only 3 weeks of partial relief.
- An MRI on June 29, 2026 showed a complete mid-substance tear of my ACL with a bone bruise pattern; my menisci were intact and there was no significant arthritis.
- I have recurrent instability with pivoting and my knee has given way twice on stairs.
- On exam, I had positive provocative testing on the affected side and limited range of motion due to pain.

**What the plan's policy says:**
The policy I was given excerpts of states that "Coverage Rationale Surgery of the knee is proven and medically necessary in certain circumstances," and that "For medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the InterQual® CP." It also states that "Medical records documentation may be required to assess whether the member meets the clinical criteria for coverage but does not guarantee coverage of the service requested," and that "UnitedHealthcare may also use tools developed by third parties, such as the InterQual® criteria, to assist us in administering health benefits."

I want to be straightforward with the plan: I have not been given, and cannot quote, any specific language from the plan's own policy that sets out a required duration, type, or number of conservative-care attempts specifically for ACL reconstruction. The excerpts I have address unicondylar/patellofemoral knee replacement, articular cartilage repair, meniscal allografts, and general references to InterQual criteria — not a stated conservative-care threshold for CPT 29888. If such a specific criterion exists, it is contained in the InterQual® criteria referenced by the policy, which I have not been provided.

Based on the record, I completed a documented course of supervised physical therapy, medication management, and an injection, all without lasting relief, before my surgeon recommended surgery. I am asking the plan to explain, in writing, exactly what conservative-care criterion in the InterQual guidelines it applied, and how my records fell short of it — because nothing in the excerpts I have been given describes that standard.

## Request for the Specific Criteria Applied

Because this denial relies on InterQual® criteria, which is licensed software and not a public document, I am formally requesting that UnitedHealthcare provide me, free of charge, with the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination. I understand that under ERISA and ACA appeal rules, I have the right to receive the specific rule or criterion the plan relied on in denying my claim, and I am asking for that documentation now so that I can respond to it fully.

## Deadline and Where I Am Sending This Appeal

I understand my appeal must be received by January 29, 2027, though I recognize the date on my denial letter is authoritative if it differs. I am submitting this appeal by signing in at member.uhc.com and/or by calling the number on my member ID card, and I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, as instructed.

## What I Am Asking For

I am asking UnitedHealthcare to reconsider this denial, to review the clinical documentation described above together with my surgeon's records, and to provide me with the specific InterQual criteria applied to my case so that I can understand and, if needed, further respond to the basis for this decision.

Thank you for your time and attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

**Quinn Grant**
Member ID: W553544386
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
[Date of signature]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
